editorial:
The Fighting Marines is a 1935 Mascot Pictures serial. Wikipedia lists a release date of November 23, 1935, directors B. Reeves Eason and Joseph Kane, and a cast led by Grant Withers as Corporal Larry Lawrence, with Ann Rutherford, Adrian Morris and Robert Warwick. It lists 12 chapters (216 minutes), including 'Human Targets' and 'Two Against the Horde'. Wikipedia also describes it as the last serial produced by Mascot Pictures. Those details come from Wikipedia. A creator might want it for a cliffhanger sequence or period Marine Corps imagery.

The rights trap is that its status is unproven. A 1935 film is protected unless its copyright was not renewed in the year-28 window, 1962–63. My partial look at the 1962–1964 Catalog of Copyright Entries volumes found no renewal, but I did not read them in full. Those volumes are the authoritative source for 1960s renewals. The Copyright Office online catalog covers 1978 onward and would at most show later-filed records. Treat the print as unresolved until a reviewer reads the 1962 and 1963 volumes in full. The serial is hosted on the Internet Archive as a community upload, but hosting is not a rights finding. Any uploader's titles, music or edits are separate matters.
faq: Is The Fighting Marines (1935) free to reuse?

Not yet confirmed. It is a 1935 film, so it is free only if its copyright was not renewed. A partial check of the 1962–1964 catalog volumes found no renewal, but the check was incomplete. The 1962 and 1963 volumes are the ones that matter, and 1964 is only a late-filing margin.
Can I use the Internet Archive copy?

The Internet Archive item, a 2021 community upload, lists 12 chapter files. I did not check that they are complete or play correctly. Hosting does not settle rights. Finish the renewal check first. Then look at what the uploader added, such as titles, music or edits.
